cells.tense: Nurturing is settled here, and the pen stays in the hand while it works.
cells.ask: Watch one thing you're tending today. Leave it one beat longer than your own twitch wants, and see how it does on its own.
cells.core:
The structure in front of you came down and nothing needed pushing. What's left is ground you can work with, and you're holding it loosely — no grip, no steering. So the small thing on top grows at its own rate, and the care you offer doesn't eat you. That's the whole of it: room given, room used.

What tends to happen next is quiet. The unfinished thing moves on a schedule that isn't yours, and you're not spending yourself to make that true. Keep the grip off and this holds. Tending, not delivering — that's the difference you're living in right now. Let something grow without your help in the room, so the help stays honest when you do give it.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the room, not the outcome, and it's working.
cells.place: A place where false structure has just come down

cells.tense: The care is running ahead of the clearing, and it will not wait for the ground to settle.
cells.ask: Pull one hand off the rubble today. Leave whatever you were managing to settle on its own, and let the mess be unmanaged until tomorrow.
cells.core:
Care works here when the thing being tended gets to set its own pace. You give it room, check in, and step back — the growth is not on your clock. That much is available in this seat.

What's happening instead is that you're ahead of it. Somewhere forward is a version where everything underneath is solid again, and you can't stop working toward it. So care becomes management — clearing debris, propping what hasn't fallen, steering what's already loose. Nobody asked for that. Standing in the open with no hand on anything feels like the bigger drop, and so the hand stays on. The fixing costs you the clearing itself. Let one hand come off.
cells.sheetLine: You're propping up what's already coming down.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door the clearing already opened, and it shut behind you.
cells.ask: Put water on one thing you've stopped tending. Look at it once a week, and leave the growth rate alone.
cells.core:
The clearing happened. Whatever fell, fell — that part is finished. But the caring hasn't come back with you. You show it as not needing help, and that's the wall doing its work. Little is growing around you now, not because the ground is bad. The offer to look after one thing — a plant, a person, a small piece of your own life — quietly stopped being made.

The way back runs through what pulls you. Find something that clearly wants to live, and let your attention be drawn toward it. You don't have to feel nurturing first. Follow the pull toward one living thing, and care for it follows on its own.
cells.sheetLine: The door's behind you now. The caring hasn't come back yet.

cells.tense: Somebody's hands are doing the nurturing, and the account of it hasn't been signed.
cells.ask: Catch one act of care you've been filing as basic upkeep. Say plainly who it's for, once.
cells.core:
People around you are growing. They grow in a space someone holds open, and that someone is you — in how you listen, how you sit next to somebody, how you make the room safe enough to fall apart in. You call that being practical. The care does real work, and you've been treating it as just what people do.

Nothing here needs an opinion. What's left is noticing what you're already carrying. Take one act you've been calling basic upkeep and say it's yours. Then it's a choice you can make, instead of a weight that's there because it's there.
cells.sheetLine: The care is already working. You haven't claimed it yet.
